subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation: latency & throughput SLOs
messages:

Subject: Dedicated capacity performance validation: latency & throughput SLOs

Hi Ellen
- great to meet you on the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side: 

Summary of SLOs you mentioned:
- Streaming responses (server-sent events) for chat UI
- Target p50 latency: <= 150ms (per response)
- Target p95 latency: <= 300ms for typical traffic, allow short spikes up to 350-400ms
- Average request payload: ~512 tokens in, ~350 tokens out (we'll validate with traces)
- Typical concurrency: 50 concurrent users; observed spikes up to 150 during peak promotions
- Desired reserved throughput: baseline to cover 200 rps with ability to burst to 400 rps

Open questions for sizing and validation:
1) Do you have a representative workload trace you can share (timestamps + token counts)?
2) Are you comfortable with a canary/deployment window where we run the dedicated pool under your traffic for 48-72 hours?
3) Any hard budget caps for dedicated GPU pools we should keep in mind?

Next steps we propose:
- Please share a workload trace (anonymized) - we can run it through our benchmark harness.
- We'll produce a short perf matrix comparing Nvidia A100 vs H100 (and a lower-cost option) with expected p95/p50 and reserved throughput sizing.
- If the perf matrix looks good, provision a 72-hour canary on dedicated capacity to validate under real traffic.

Attachment: workload_trace_0519.csv (csv, ~1.2MB) - please confirm if this is okay to use.

Thanks - I’ll loop Marissa and Aditya in for the perf sizing and canary plan.
— Alex

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation: latency & throughput SLOs

Hi Ellen - thanks for the trace. We ran a quick pass through our internal harness overnight and have an initial, high-level perf matrix and recommendation (attached). Key takeaways: 

High-level GPU comparison (preliminary):
- NVIDIA A100 (80GB)
  - Expected baseline p50: ~120-160ms (single-request streaming), p95: ~260-330ms depending on sequence length
  - Baseline reserved throughput: ~180-220 rps for your workload profile (with 8 multi-request concurrent streams per GPU instance)
  - Cost: mid-range for dedicated pools
- NVIDIA H100 (80GB)
  - Expected baseline p50: ~90-120ms, p95: ~200-260ms (better kernel efficiency for attention ops)
  - Baseline reserved throughput: ~260-320 rps for same profile (roughly 1.3-1.5x A100)
  - Recommended if p95 target <= 300ms is strict under sustained concurrency
- Lower-cost/Inference-optimized (e.g., L4 / 48GB Ampere-like)
  - Much lower cost but p95 often degrades ~1.5-2x vs A100; suitable for non-critical routes or caching-heavy workloads

Streaming considerations:
- Continuous batching improves throughput but can add ~10-40ms tail latency if not carefully tuned. For SSE we bias toward low-latency (smaller batch windows) and prefix caching to reduce repeated compute.
- KV cache warmup: recommend a short pre-warm phase for hot prefixes; we'll instrument and report hit rates during canary.

Recommended reserved sizing for canary (initial):
- Provision H100 pool sized for 320 rps reserved with autoscaling headroom to 480 rps for short bursts (10-20m).
- Canary window: 72 hours with production traffic split 20% to the canary pool initially, ramp to 50% if metrics look good.

Deliverables attached: redwood_perf_matrix_20270601.pdf (PDF, 2 pages) and mvp_canary_plan_20270601.md (Markdown plan).

If you’re comfortable with H100 recommended baseline, we can request provisioning and schedule a canary workshop. Alex - can you confirm procurement constraints and preferred canary dates?

Thanks,
 Marissa
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Date: Wed, 02 Jun 2027 15:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity performance validation: latency & throughput SLOs

Ellen - thanks for the quick review and Marissa for the clear recommendations. Quick operational notes and proposed timeline: 

Operational ask:
- If Shopwell Procurement can provision a short approval (~PO or chargeback) for a 3-day H100 canary, we'll provision a dedicated pool and run real-traffic validation. We typically request a provisioning lead time of 24-48 hours.

Proposed timeline:
- Thu 2027-06-03: finalize procurement approval and sign off on canary plan (mvp_canary_plan_20270601.md).
- Fri 2027-06-04: provision H100 dedicated pool (baseline reserved 320 rps, burst to 480 rps).
- Mon- Wed 2027-06-07 to 2027-06-09: 72-hour canary with staged traffic (20% -> 50%).
- Thu 2027-06-10: wrap-up metrics review and decisions (scale, buy, tuning).

Metrics we will capture during canary (dashboard links included in the plan): p50/p95 latency, tail percentiles (p99), request success rate, per-token cost, and streaming frame delays. We will also instrument KV cache hit rates and per-route CPU/GPU utilization.

If procurement has any hard budget limits, we can provide an alternate A100-based plan with lower cost and slightly relaxed p95 expectation. Otherwise we recommend H100 to hit the <300ms p95 target under sustained load.

Ellen - can you confirm whether procurement can approve the short canary budget and if the proposed timeline looks feasible? Happy to jump on a 15-min sync to close this out.

 Aditya
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
aditya.rao@redwood.ai
